stories.notes: Multi-platform live preview feature with no acceptance criteria. High complexity: real-time rendering, state synchronization, platform-specific concerns (GO, UP, MX). Openspec must elaborate AC and technical depth first; speckit then hardens with testability, security, and edge-case coverage.

agentContributions.notes: Story requests a new Live Preview capability for Contentstack CMS content. No acceptance criteria provided; VCs derived from the title/description. The attachment point is useContent (236 callers) and its backing provider — the single funnel through which all Contentstack content flows. Cannot see useContent source or its provider, so location is inferred from the call graph. Live preview likely requires integrating Contentstack's preview SDK/webhook at the provider layer so that content updates propagate to consuming components without a full page reload.

Openspec provided empty acceptance criteria, so all ACs are authored from scratch based on the story title ('Live Preview of Content in CMS'), the three affected codebases (GO, UP, MX), and the identified integration points (useContent, ContentstackContext). FILE CONTENTS WERE NOT AVAILABLE for review — criteria are derived from titles, paths, and the story description alone. This is a significant caveat: the actual structure of useContent and ContentstackContext may reveal additional content types, error paths, or configuration mechanisms that should be covered. ACs should be validated against source code once reviewable. Key areas covered: (1) core live-preview propagation (AC-1, AC-2), (2) user-facing preview indicator (AC-3), (3) fallback when preview is unavailable (AC-4), (4) reconnection resilience (AC-5), (5) production isolation / security (AC-6), (6) cross-site consistency (AC-7), (7) content-type coverage for named interfaces (AC-8), (8) malformed data error handling (AC-9), (9) preview exit behavior (AC-10), (10) rapid-update performance (AC-11), (11) create/delete edge cases (AC-12).

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: All four manifest paths exist (useContent.ts, ContentstackContext.tsx, contentCard.ts, ContentstackLink.tsx) — no missing files. Both agents added non-overlapping value: openspec identified the integration architecture (useContent as the single funnel for 236 callers, ContentstackContext as the provider layer) and inferred the preview-SDK integration point; speckit then authored 12 acceptance criteria covering propagation, UI indicators, fallback, reconnection, production isolation, cross-site consistency, content-type coverage, malformed data, preview exit, rapid-update performance, and create/delete edge cases. HOWEVER: both agents explicitly state that file contents were NOT available — openspec inferred location from the call graph alone, and speckit authored all 12 ACs blind from titles, paths, and the story description. Speckit itself flags this as 'a significant caveat' and recommends validating ACs against source code once reviewable. Additionally, there is a metadata inconsistency: speckit reports acceptanceChanged=false despite stating it authored all ACs from scratch (the original acceptanceCriteria array was empty). For a brownfield ticket where ACs are immutable, authoring new ACs with acceptanceChanged=false is contradictory — either the ACs were not actually persisted (and thus the spec output is incomplete) or the flag is wrong. Human review is required to (1) validate the 12 ACs against actual source code structure, content types, and error paths in useContent/ContentstackContext, and (2) reconcile the acceptanceChanged metadata.
